source.title: Fine-Grained Manipulation of Arithmetic Neurons
source.authors: Wen-Yu Du; Rui Zheng; Tongxu Luo; Stephen Chung; Jie Fu

record.tranche_reason: The study builds on prior findings about arithmetic heuristic neurons and uses them for targeted manipulation of arithmetic outputs. Its reported results do not measure whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs or how common polysemanticity is.
record.gate_note: The study reports arithmetic-heuristic classification, ablation, activation manipulation, and SNR results. These concern neuron-level arithmetic control, not the claim versions' measures of polysemanticity, unrelated inputs, or its prevalence; the relevant findings are recorded under fits_no_version. The prior-work claims about arithmetic neurons are cited, not new results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study localizes arithmetic MLP neurons in Llama-3 models, ranks them by importance to result-digit heuristics, and steers addition outputs by editing activations. It never measures whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs or how common that is, and has no capacity, architecture or measurement comparison bearing on V1–V7. It only assumes superposition to explain off-target ablation effects and imperfect manipulation, without testing it. It does not rely on polysemanticity as a tool either, so T6 fits better than T4.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that a linear classifier can rank arithmetic neurons by heuristic importance. Editing about 50 top-ranked neurons steers addition outputs to target digit patterns (over 80% for the ones place). Top neurons have 'cleaner channels' shown by higher SNR. They also report correcting some wrong predictions and small gains from operand heuristics.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses arithmetic-neuron localization, linear heuristic classifiers, and activation edits; it does not test the original sources' polysemanticity methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Manipulation success varies by result digit place, source-target heuristic pair, model, and K. The reported classification result also differs between the maximum-activation approach and the trained classifier.

fits_no_version.finding: Zeroing top-ranked neurons for one ones-place heuristic sharply lowers accuracy on matching prompts but also mildly lowers it on other prompts. The authors attribute the off-target drop, and the imperfect manipulation, to superposition without testing this (Figure 3, Limitations).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Arithmetic heuristic neurons in Llama3-8B are not fully heuristic-specific; ablating them has mild off-target effects on other heuristics.

fits_no_version.finding: The max-activation matching method assigns only 20% (66/320) of arithmetic neurons to any result heuristic. A linear classifier on all 320 activations separates heuristics with over 90% accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Assigning arithmetic neurons to heuristics depends on the method: top-activation matching versus distributed linear readout.

fits_no_version.finding: Editing K=50 ranked neurons steers Llama3-8B addition outputs to target ones-place (81.4%) and tens-place (68.1%) patterns. Success is lower for the hundreds place and for other model sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Heuristic-ranked arithmetic neurons causally steer specific output patterns in Llama-3 models.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 8th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: The paper says manipulation is not perfect and hypothesizes superposition as a cause. The main analysis uses addition and models whose number tokenization combines digits; it notes conclusions might differ for models that tokenize single digits. Some additional results are reported only as aggregate table averages or figure descriptions.
record.rows_left_out: The individual source-target manipulation rates in Tables 1–6 are not transcribed separately; the rows record the aggregate values stated in the text or table averages. Those detailed pairwise rates concern arithmetic steering, not any tested claim version.

untested.parts: Vision models; no image classifiers studied.
Share of LLM MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, and its layer dependence. Only arithmetic-relevant neurons on arithmetic prompts are studied.
Superposition as a cause of polysemanticity; it is invoked as an assumption only.
Effects of activation function, architecture or regularization on the polysemantic share.
Whether apparently mixed neurons detect one shared feature.
Measurement dependence of polysemantic classification. The max-activation versus classifier contrast concerns heuristic assignment, not polysemanticity.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4/uses_without_test is close; I chose assumes/T6 because polysemanticity is neither used as a tool nor tested, only invoked as superposition to explain imperfection. All rows correctly map to none. The text notes a neuron may be associated with several heuristics (from Nikankin et al.), but no prevalence is measured.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure the prevalence of neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts; its heuristic classes concern arithmetic result patterns.
Superposition as a cause of polysemanticity or capacity pressure relative to feature count.
Polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure from initialization, regularization, or training noise.
Changes in polysemantic-neuron share due to activation function, architecture, or regularization, and performance costs.
Whether canonical mixed-response neurons detect a shared feature or related jobs rather than unrelated inputs.
Whether the measurement choices described in this version change which neurons count as polysemantic.
